name: Primeval History
summary: Creation, the fall, the flood and Babel (Gen 1–11). Dates here are not recoverable from the text and are shown only as a span.

name: The Patriarchs
summary: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph: the family of promise moves from Ur to Canaan to Egypt (Gen 12–50).

name: Egypt & Exodus
summary: Israel grows in Egypt, is enslaved, and is brought out under Moses; covenant at Sinai and forty years in the wilderness. The exodus date is debated (c. 1446 vs c. 1260 BC).

name: Conquest & Judges
summary: Joshua leads Israel into Canaan; a cycle of apostasy, oppression and deliverance follows under the judges.

name: United Monarchy
summary: Saul, David and Solomon rule a united Israel; Jerusalem becomes capital and the temple is built.

name: Divided Kingdom
summary: Israel (north) and Judah (south) split; prophets confront kings. Samaria falls to Assyria in 722 BC; Jerusalem to Babylon in 586 BC.

name: Exile
summary: Judah in Babylon. Daniel and Ezekiel minister among the exiles.

name: Return & Restoration
summary: Under Persian rule exiles return, rebuild the temple and walls, and renew the covenant (Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi).

name: Second Temple Period
summary: Greek and then Roman rule; Maccabean revolt (167 BC); rise of Pharisees, Sadducees and Essenes.

name: Life of Jesus
summary: Birth, ministry, death and resurrection of Jesus of Nazareth (c. 5 BC – AD 30/33).

name: Apostolic Age
summary: Pentecost, the spread of the church from Jerusalem to Rome, the letters of the New Testament, and the fall of the temple (AD 70).

name: Early Church
summary: Apostolic Fathers, apologists and martyrs; the church grows under intermittent persecution.

name: Imperial Church
summary: From Constantine to Gregory the Great: councils, creeds, Augustine and the Cappadocians.

name: Medieval Church
summary: Monasticism, the East–West schism (1054), scholasticism, penance and purgatory.

name: Reformation
summary: Luther, Zwingli, Calvin, the Anabaptists, the Catholic Reformation, Arminius and Dort.

name: Modern Era
summary: Awakenings, missions, dispensationalism, Pentecostalism and global Christianity.
